cards.front: In a throwaway container from the alpine image, mount your current host directory at `/data` so the container cannot change it, and list it
cards.topic: volumes and bind mounts: docker run -v

cards.front: Create an empty Docker-managed volume called `pgdata`, without starting any container
cards.back: `docker volume create pgdata` `docker run -v` also creates missing volumes
cards.topic: volumes and bind mounts: docker run -v

cards.front: A container edits a file that came from its image. Where does the changed version go?
cards.back: The file is first copied up into the container's writable layer and edited there (copy-on-write).
cards.topic: why files written inside a container disappear

cards.front: List the volumes Docker manages on your machine
cards.back: `docker volume ls` Bind-mounted host folders do not appear here
cards.topic: volumes and bind mounts: docker run -v

cards.front: What happens to CMD when ENTRYPOINT is written in shell form, like `ENTRYPOINT python app.py`?
cards.back: CMD is ignored, and so are any arguments passed after the image name in `docker run`.

cards.front: Do arguments after the image name in `docker run` replace ENTRYPOINT?
cards.back: No, they are appended to it; only the `--entrypoint` flag replaces ENTRYPOINT.

cards.front: Where does a running container store the files it writes?
cards.back: In its own thin writable layer, stacked on top of the image's read-only layers.
cards.topic: why files written inside a container disappear

cards.front: When a Dockerfile sets both ENTRYPOINT and CMD in exec form, what does CMD become?
cards.back: Default arguments added to the end of ENTRYPOINT, used only when `docker run` passes none.

cards.front: Show the details of the volume `redisdata`, including where on the host its files live
cards.back: `docker volume inspect redisdata` On Mac, that path is inside Docker's VM
cards.topic: volumes and bind mounts: docker run -v

cards.front: Start a container from the redis image, keeping its `/data` directory in a Docker-managed volume called `redisdata`
cards.back: `docker run -v redisdata:/data redis` A name without a slash means volume, not folder
cards.topic: volumes and bind mounts: docker run -v

cards.front: Why can't a new container from the same image see files written by an earlier one?
cards.back: Each container gets its own fresh, empty writable layer; only the read-only image layers are shared.
cards.topic: why files written inside a container disappear

cards.front: Does stopping a container delete the files written inside it?
cards.back: No: stopping keeps its writable layer; only removing the container, e.g. with `docker rm`, deletes those files.
cards.topic: why files written inside a container disappear

cards.front: What happens to an image's CMD when you add arguments after the image name in `docker run`?
cards.back: They replace CMD completely; nothing from the original CMD is kept.

cards.front: Do ENTRYPOINT and CMD run during `docker build`, like RUN does?
cards.back: No, they only record what to run; it runs when a container starts.

cards.front: How do you keep a container's data after the container is removed?
cards.back: Write it to a volume or bind mount, which lives outside the container's writable layer.
cards.topic: why files written inside a container disappear
